newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end lower on rail budget speculation.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end lower on rail budget speculation.

text.p: Delhi shares closed lower on Monday after early gains as speculators unloaded shares expecting a hike in railway freight rates in the railway budget scheduled to be presented later this week, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 7.31 points lower at 718.55.
Brokers said the absence of institutional buyers also aided the fall in share prices.
"Most of the institutional investors adopted a wait-and-watch strategy, which made the fall steeper," said one broker.
Another broker said: "The pre-budget panic selling was triggered by fears that the government would sharply increase the freight charges of railways in the railway budget."
The Indian government is due to present the railway budget 1997/98 (April-March) on Wednesday and the general budget for the same period on Friday.
"Marketmen sold on fears that the Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's budgetary proposals may fall short of market expectations," said Manoj Choraria of brokers Choraria Associates.
Reliance Industries closed 4.95 rupees lower at 257.45 on profit-taking by speculators, brokers said.
State Bank of India shed 6.30 rupees, falling to 275.80, on selling by foreign institutional investors.
